input.plan:
# Multi-month navigation + Year-to-Date rollup

## Context

The app (`personal-finance-app`, JavaFX, package `com.example.finance`) currently pins every month-scoped view to `YearMonth.now()` with no way to look at a different month — `MonthSummaryView` and `CategorySummaryView` have an unused `YearMonth`-parameterized constructor that `MainApp` never calls, and `TransactionEntryView.refreshTransactions()` hardcodes `YearMonth.now()` inline with no override at all. There's also no rollup wider than a single month anywhere in `BudgetService`/`MonthSummaryService`. The user wants to be able to navigate across months and see a year-to-date rollup, so this plan adds (1) one shared month-navigation control driving the three month-scoped tabs, and (2) a YTD section added to the existing Month Summary tab.

Decisions already confirmed with the user:
- **Month nav**: one shared Prev/Next/Today control above the `TabPane`, driving Month Summary, Transactions, and Categories together. Savings Goals and Recurring Obligations are not month-scoped today and stay untouched.
- **YTD placement**: a new section inside the existing Month Summary tab (not a new tab), rolling up January through the currently selected month, for that month's year.

## Implementation

### 1. Shared month state + nav bar — `MainApp.java`
Add `ObjectProperty<YearMonth> selectedMonth = new SimpleObjectProperty<>(YearMonth.now())` in `start()`, constructed before the views. Add a private `buildMonthNavigationBar(selectedMonth)` returning an `HBox` with Previous/Today/Next `Button`s (`minusMonths(1)` / `YearMonth.now()` / `plusMonths(1)`) and a `Label` (format `MMMM yyyy`) kept in sync via a listener on `selectedMonth`. Wrap the existing `TabPane` in a `VBox` with this bar above it.

Pass `selectedMonth` into the three month-scoped view constructors (see below). Add a second listener on `selectedMonth`, parallel to the existing tab-switch listener, calling `refresh()` on exactly `monthSummaryView`, `transactionEntryView`, `categorySummaryView` (not the Savings Goals / Recurring Obligations views).

### 2. Views take the shared property instead of a fixed `YearMonth`
- `MonthSummaryView`, `CategorySummaryView`: replace the `final YearMonth month` field with `ReadOnlyObjectProperty<YearMonth> selectedMonth`; remove the now-dead no-arg-month convenience constructor; `refresh()` reads `selectedMonth.get()` at call time instead of the stored field.
- `TransactionEntryView`: add a `ReadOnlyObjectProperty<YearMonth> selectedMonth` constructor param and field; in `refreshTransactions()` replace `YearMonth currentMonth = YearMonth.now();` with `YearMonth currentMonth = selectedMonth.get();`.

Reading the property at call time (rather than caching a `YearMonth`) is required because `refresh()` fires from three different triggers (tab switch, month-nav change, each view's own "Refresh" button) and must always reflect whatever month is currently selected.

### 3. `BudgetService` — generalize to a range, add YTD category totals
Generalize the private filter to `sumTransactions(YearMonth from, YearMonth to, TransactionType type, String categoryName)` (inclusive range via `YearMonth.isBefore`/`isAfter`). Keep `totalIncome(month)`/`totalExpenses(month)`/`leftover(month)` as thin delegates to new `(from, to)` overloads (`from = to = month`), so single-month behavior and tests are unaffected while both paths share one filter.

Add YTD category totals as their own method/type rather than overloading `CategoryTotal` (whose `getRemaining()`/`isOverBudget()` are hardcoded to a single month's `monthlyTarget` — reusing it across a range would silently misrepresent budget-vs-actual):
```java
public static class YtdCategoryTotal {
    // category, actual, scaledTarget, incomeOnly
    // getRemaining() = scaledTarget.subtract(actual)
    // isOverBudget() = actual.compareTo(scaledTarget) > 0
}

public List<YtdCategoryTotal> categoryTotalsYearToDate(YearMonth throughMonth) {
    // from = YearMonth.of(throughMonth.getYear(), 1)
    // scaledTarget = category.getMonthlyTarget() * throughMonth.getMonthValue()
}
```
Scaling the monthly target by months-elapsed keeps YTD over/under-budget an apples-to-apples comparison (otherwise YTD would either trivially always look under-budget or lose the over/under signal the monthly view already gives users).

### 4. `MonthSummaryService` — new `summarizeYearToDate`
Add `summarizeYearToDate(YearMonth month)` returning a new nested `YearToDateSummary` (mirrors `MonthSummary`'s shape): `year`, `throughMonth`, `monthsElapsed`, `categoryTotals` (`List<BudgetService.YtdCategoryTotal>`), `totalIncome`, `totalExpenses`, `leftover`, `overBudgetCount`. Built from `budgetService.categoryTotalsYearToDate(month)` and `budgetService.totalIncome/totalExpenses/leftover(Jan-of-year, month)`. Deliberately independent of `SavingsGoalService`/`RecurringObligationService` — those aren't month-scoped and are out of scope here.

### 5. `MonthSummaryView` — YTD section UI
Add a `Separator`, `ytdHeaderLabel`, `ytdSummaryLabel` (income/expenses/leftover, same `String.format` style as the existing leftover label), `ytdWarningLabel` (same over-budget-count phrasing as the existing warning label, worded for "YTD target"), and a `ytdChartsBox` holding one new `BarChart` (scaled target vs. YTD actual, built the same way as the existing `buildBarChart`, skipping income-only categories). No second pie chart — it would duplicate the monthly one with no new information. Call `monthSummaryService.summarizeYearToDate(month)` inside `refresh()` alongside the existing `summarize(month, today)` call and populate these new elements.

### 6. `CategorySummaryView`
Constructor-only change: take `ReadOnlyObjectProperty<YearMonth> selectedMonth`; `refresh()` calls `budgetService.categoryTotals(selectedMonth.get())`; remove the dead no-arg-month constructor.

## Tests

`BudgetServiceTest.java` — add: multi-month range sums only include months within `[from, to]`; a single-month range call matches the pre-existing single-arg result (delegation sanity check); `categoryTotalsYearToDate` scales target by months elapsed; over-budget boundary at the scaled target (equal → false, one cent over → true); January YTD equals the plain single-month `categoryTotals`; a prior-year transaction is excluded from YTD.

`MonthSummaryServiceTest.java` — add: `summarizeYearToDate` aggregates only the target year's Jan-through-selected-month transactions; over-budget count reflects the *scaled* target (a category over its single-month target every month but under its scaled YTD target is not flagged, and vice versa); January's YTD summary matches the plain single-month summary exactly.

No new UI test files — consistent with the current codebase, which has no `*ViewTest` classes.

## Verification

1. `mvn test` — all existing + new tests pass.
2. `mvn javafx:run` — confirm the nav bar shows the current month and all three tabs default to it as before.
3. Click Previous twice: nav label updates, and Month Summary (incl. new YTD section), Transactions, and Categories all update without needing to switch tabs.
4. Click Today from a different month: snaps back to the real current month.
5. Savings Goals / Recurring Obligations tabs are unaffected by month nav, still only refresh on tab switch.
6. In a month with several months of same-category history, compare the monthly bar chart's target (1x) against the YTD bar chart's scaled target (Nx) for the same category.
7. Navigate to January and confirm the YTD numbers match the monthly numbers exactly.

### Critical files
- `personal-finance-app/src/main/java/com/example/finance/MainApp.java`
- `personal-finance-app/src/main/java/com/example/finance/BudgetService.java`
- `personal-finance-app/src/main/java/com/example/finance/MonthSummaryService.java`
- `personal-finance-app/src/main/java/com/example/finance/MonthSummaryView.java`
- `personal-finance-app/src/main/java/com/example/finance/TransactionEntryView.java`
- `personal-finance-app/src/main/java/com/example/finance/CategorySummaryView.java`
- `personal-finance-app/src/test/java/com/example/finance/BudgetServiceTest.java`
- `personal-finance-app/src/test/java/com/example/finance/MonthSummaryServiceTest.java`

Compiles clean. Everything is implemented and verified:

- **`BudgetService`**: generalized single-month sums into range-based sums (`totalIncome/totalExpenses/leftover(from, to)`), added `categoryTotalsYearToDate` with a new `YtdCategoryTotal` type (target scaled by months elapsed).
- **`MonthSummaryService`**: added `summarizeYearToDate` / `YearToDateSummary`.
- **`MonthSummaryView`**: added a YTD section (income/expenses/leftover, over-budget warning, target-vs-actual bar chart) below the existing monthly dashboard.
- **`TransactionEntryView`** / **`CategorySummaryView`**: now read the shared selected month instead of hardcoding `YearMonth.now()`.
- **`MainApp`**: added a shared `YearMonth` property with a Previous/Today/Next navigation bar above the tabs, wired to refresh Month Summary, Transactions, and Categories on change (Savings Goals and Recurring Obligations are untouched, as decided).
- Added 6 new tests to `BudgetServiceTest` and 3 to `MonthSummaryServiceTest` covering range sums, YTD scaling/boundaries, and January-equals-single-month invariants. All 65 tests pass, and `mvn javafx:run` launches cleanly with no exceptions.

One caveat: I verified the app launches without errors but couldn't visually click through the Prev/Next/Today buttons or eyeball the new YTD chart layout — worth a quick manual pass (`mvn javafx:run`) to confirm the UI looks right.
